note: Curated public copy only: the words a person has to choose. Nothing here is a value the build can derive -- titles, counts, digests, versions, licences and paths are read from the ontology, the layout contract and the pins at build time, because a figure typed here is a second description that can drift from the first.

site.name: Business Capability Ontology
site.tagline: What an organization can do, as BFO dispositions realized in business processes

draft.text: The Business Capability Ontology is under development and has not been released. Its v0.5 specification commitments were ratified under CP-0. Forty-two specific Business Capability types have passed G1-T admission. Thirty-nine of those types, together with the generic Business Capability parent, are implemented as OWL classes in the first Stage 05 tranche. The implementation has passed its reported class-level validation against pinned partial ontology extracts. Instance-level validation, CP-1/CP-2 completion, and full upstream ontology conformance remain outstanding. No production knowledge graph or ontology release has been approved.
draft.why: A validator reading a requirement on a public site will reasonably take it as settled. Every page says otherwise, because the one page that does not is the one somebody links to.

iri_resolution.text: BCO IRIs identify terms but do not resolve over HTTP yet. The namespace https://fandaws.com/ontology/bco# is permanent; serving it is a release obligation. Use the explorer or the downloads to inspect a term.
iri_resolution.why: An IRI rendered as a link would send a reader to a 404 and imply the ontology is broken. IRIs are copyable text, never anchors.

license.text: Project-authored ontology, documentation and site content are offered under the MIT License. The vendored BFO, CCO and BPO extracts carry their own licences (CC BY 4.0, BSD-3-Clause, MIT) and attribution, listed on the Modules and Downloads pages. The Models page renders its diagrams with a vendored copy of Mermaid (MIT), credited on the Downloads page.
license.why: A licence printed without the upstream exception reads as covering everything on the page, including terms this project did not write -- and, since the Models page, a script this project did not write.

acknowledgment.text: Developed by Aaron Damiano with substantial assistance from Anthropic Claude and OpenAI ChatGPT agents.
acknowledgment.why: Carried from ValueNet's practice: the assistance was substantive, so it is credited on every page rather than in a footnote most readers never reach. The human author is the one answerable for the content.

vocabulary_empty.text: No vocabulary concept has been written yet. The metamodel and catalog concepts arrive in P5, all as Draft; until then both schemes are declared and empty.
vocabulary_empty.why: An empty scheme with no explanation reads as a broken build. The plan stage that fills it is the architect's (P5 of the approved plan), so it is words a person chose rather than a figure the build can read.

models.text: Diagrams are rendered in your browser from the Mermaid source shown with each one; with JavaScript off, the source is what you see, and it is the diagram. No model is approved until its own Review status says so.
models.why: The Mermaid source in the model file is the truth (docs/decisions/2026-10-25-stage-02-choices.md), so a reader should know the picture is drawn from it rather than drawn separately. And a model on a public site reads as settled; whether it is approved is stated in the model, and the page says where to look.

models_empty.text: No conceptual model has been written yet. CM-01, the Business Capability Conceptual Domain Model, is the first planned; it appears here when it is committed.
models_empty.why: An empty page with no explanation reads as a broken build. That CM-01 comes first is the architect's choice (docs/decisions/2026-10-25-stage-02-choices.md), so it is words a person chose rather than a figure the build can read.

ratification.text: Specification v0.5.0-draft.3 is the specification in force. Its commitments were ratified under CP-0 by the decision records below, which control; the table that follows is the specification's own register, as it stands at this commit. Ratification settles what the design commits to. It does not mean any requirement has passed executable validation: the Validation section below says what the checks currently find.
ratification.why: The architect's direction of 2026-11-15 (B): the specification's ratification status is linked to the controlling CP-0 records, and it must not read as a claim that every requirement has passed executable validation. The list is words a person chose; the build refuses a path that is not a decision record.

build_label.why: A Pages build is not a release. The source commit is shown beside this label.

home.summary: The Business Capability Ontology (BCO) says what an organization can do. The Business Process Ontology (BPO) says what it does. The BCO takes its act types from the BPO reality layer and adds the dispositions those acts realize.
for_validators: Read the specification. It states seventeen design decisions (CD1 to CD17), the requirements that would check them (CAP-01 onward), and the ten ratification points (RP-1 to RP-10) through which the architect ratified them.
Explore the terms. Today the explorer holds the upstream BFO, CCO and BPO terms the specification builds on, each marked upstream. BCO terms appear beside them as they are written.
Check the status page for what has been ratified, what the validation gate currently finds, and which terms the specification names that nothing yet defines.
Raise anything you find as an issue in the repository. A finding with the section or term it concerns is the most useful kind.
